one_month_reasoning: Inside the 2026-11-05 window: (1) Nokia's Q3 2026 interim report on 22 Oct 2026 (financial calendar, src 3) - yes, the next quarterly report falls inside the window. Management guided Q3 net sales +3% to +7% q/q and comparable operating profit 'largely flat' vs Q2's EUR 434m, then a meaningful Q4 step-up, and said it is tracking 'somewhat above the midpoint' of the EUR 2.1-2.6bn FY26 range (src 1). Infront consensus (4 Aug) has Q3 comparable EBIT EUR 444m and EPS EUR 0.06 (src 4), slightly above the 'flat' guide, so the bar is roughly met rather than low. (2) FOMC 27-28 Oct: Kalshi 82.5% hold / 17.5% hike, Polymarket 82.5% / 16.5% (snapshot dated 6 Oct 2026, no volume shown, src 23); hike risk is a modest negative for high-multiple AI-networking names. Base rates: over the last 8 reports NOK's earnings-day move averaged 6.3% in absolute terms (-2.7, +5.9, -8.5, -4.0, +11.2, -7.8, +4.8, -5.4%; 3 up, 5 down; src 21), so earnings adds a jump of about +/-6% on top of normal drift. The stock is up ~6.3% today (driver not identified in company news) after a ~50% peak-to-trough fall from the June high of $17.45; I take no directional view from that and center the 1-month distribution at ~$10.80 (essentially today's close) with a log sd of ~14% plus a 20% fat-tail mixture (sd 24%), between the stock's long-run monthly vol (~12.5%) and the brief's realized-vol rule (62%/3.5 = 17.7%).

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 21x NTM-at-horizon comparable EPS EUR 0.4325 = EUR 9.08 = $10.23 (weight 0.65) and (b) 21x 2028 EPS implied by management's 2028 EBIT target midpoint, EUR 0.393 = EUR 8.25 = $9.29 (weight 0.35); EUR converted at EUR/USD 1.12605 (Twelve Data, 6 Oct 2026), 1 ADS = 1 share.

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis consensus 'EPS Next Year 0.41' (EUR, 25 analysts, updated 17 Sep 2026)
Infront post-Q2 consensus EUR 0.34 (range 0.32-0.36), matches StockAnalysis 0.34

2027E EUR 0.41 grown ~7%. Consensus 2027 EPS 0.41 already implies comparable EBIT of ~EUR 3.0bn ((0.41 x 5.80bn diluted shares / (1-0.265)) - EUR 0.2bn financial income), i.e. the midpoint of the 2028 target EUR 2.7-3.2bn a year early; 2028 EPS 0.44 implies ~EUR 3.27bn, just above the top of the target, capturing AI & Cloud order momentum (EUR 2.8bn Q2 orders) but well below StockAnalysis's 19.1% 3Y EPS CAGR.
Midpoint of comparable income tax rate guidance ~26-27%

Peer median forward P/E 23.5x (range 14.7-51.8x, 12 peers). ~56% of Nokia sales are Mobile Infrastructure (RAN + licensing) whose closest peer ERIC trades at 16.6x with negative EPS growth; Network Infrastructure (optical/IP/fixed) is closer to CSCO 21.9x / CIEN 41.8x / ANET 44.5x but at an 8.1% segment margin (Q2) vs much higher peer margins. Sales-weighted blend ~0.56 x 16.6 + 0.44 x ~27 = ~21x. Inside peer range, below median; no premium claimed.
Twelve Data real-time EUR/USD on 2026-10-06; Nokia's own guidance assumes 1.14 (src 1). 1 ADS = 1 share (src 25).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028 comparable EBIT at management target midpoint EUR 2.95bn + EUR 0.15bn financial income, x (1-26.5%) / 5.802bn diluted shares = EUR 0.393; x 21.0 = EUR 8.25; x 1.12605 = $9.29

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of long-term target EUR 2.7-3.2bn by 2028 (CMD, 19 Nov 2025)
Low end of 2026 guidance range, held flat

bear.story: AI/cloud optical order digestion or supply constraints cap Network Infrastructure growth, RAN stays flat, and a hawkish Fed (prediction markets ~73-75% odds of another 2026 hike per src 23) de-rates AI-networking names. Nokia is valued like Ericsson: ~15x a trimmed 2028 EPS of ~EUR 0.355 = EUR 5.33 = $6.00. Consistent with Nokia's own base rate: after its 2007 +90-100% year the stock fell 50-64% over the next 12 months (src 20).

base.story: Nokia delivers FY26 slightly above the EUR 2.35bn guidance midpoint, 2027 EPS lands near the EUR 0.41 consensus, the multiple compresses a bit toward ~21-22x NTM as the AI-networking cohort normalises; price roughly flat, in line with Nokia's long-run median 12-month return of -8% (src 20) offset by earnings growth.

bull.story: AI & Cloud orders (EUR 2.8bn in Q2 alone, about half converting within 12 months, src 1) and the San Jose / Pennsylvania / Chandler optical capacity ramp push 2028 EPS to ~EUR 0.52 and the market pays ~28x (still below CIEN/ANET/LITE) = EUR 14.6 = $16.5, near the June 2026 high of $17.45.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 14.7x (HPE) to 51.8x (LITE); trailing EV/EBITDA 7.8x (ADTN) to 123.9x (LITE). Forward EV/EBITDA was not available at the source, so the EV/EBITDA column is trailing.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 21.0x NTM comparable EPS, ~10% below the 23.5x peer median and inside the range; Nokia itself trades at 24.0x forward (src 7) and ~23.5x 2027 consensus EPS at today's EUR 9.63 per share ($10.84 / 1.12605).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount to the median, not a premium: ~56% of Nokia sales (Mobile Infrastructure, Q2'26 EUR 2,680m of 4,815m) sit in RAN/licensing, where the direct peer Ericsson trades at 16.6x with negative forecast EPS growth; Network Infrastructure grows 12-14% (guidance) at an 8.1% Q2 operating margin, below the margins and ~30%+ growth that support CIEN/ANET/LITE/COHR at 35-52x. A sales-weighted mix of the two peer groups gives ~21x.

thesis_break_reason: $7.20 is EUR 6.39, ~15.6x 2027 consensus EPS (EUR 0.41), i.e. Ericsson's multiple: the market would be pricing Nokia as a no-growth RAN vendor, which would most likely mean the AI & Cloud optical/IP growth case broke (order cancellations, a FY26 guidance cut below EUR 2.1bn, or 2027 consensus falling well below EUR 0.36). It sits ~14% below the July 2026 low of $8.37 that came on a sector sell-off without a fundamental break.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 interim report (guide: sales +3-7% q/q, comparable EBIT ~flat q/q; consensus EUR 444m / EPS EUR 0.06)
San Jose optical fab begins ramping production
FOMC meeting; prediction markets price ~73% odds of a hike, negative for high-multiple tech if delivered
Q4/FY2026 report and FY2027 outlook; test of 'somewhat above midpoint' of EUR 2.1-2.6bn
Start of leased Indium Phosphide capacity at the Chandler, Arizona site (subject to regulatory approvals)
Q1 and Q2 2027 reports: AI & Cloud order conversion (about half of Q2'26 EUR 2.8bn orders expected to convert within 12 months)

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI & Cloud optical/IP demand versus a capex digestion phase; the June-July 2026 ~50% drawdown shows how violently the cohort re-prices.
Supply constraints (management: supply is the main industry constraint) and component costs limiting conversion of the order backlog.
Whether the multiple holds near peer median when ~56% of sales are low-growth Mobile Infrastructure.
Rates: prediction markets lean toward further Fed hikes in 2026, a headwind for high-multiple networking stocks.
FX: earnings are in EUR, the ADR in USD; a 5% EUR/USD move shifts the ADR value ~5% (guidance assumes 1.14 vs 1.126 spot).
Execution of EUR 800m of 2026 restructuring charges and the China JV integration.

Defense exposure is small and not separately disclosed: Nokia reports a combined 'Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense' customer category, EUR 448m in Q2'26 (9.3% of EUR 4,815m group sales, -3% y/y; src 2). Nokia Defense was launched as an incubation unit at the Nov-2025 CMD, building on Nokia Federal Solutions (src 5). Any defense upside is optionality, not in the base case.
reasoning: Facts: last close $10.84 = EUR 9.63 per share at EUR/USD 1.12605 (Twelve Data, 6 Oct 2026; 1 ADS = 1 share). FY26 guide EUR 2.1-2.6bn comparable EBIT, management 'somewhat above the midpoint'; Q2 comparable EBIT EUR 434m (+18%), AI & Cloud sales +105%, AI & Cloud orders EUR 2.8bn; net cash EUR 2.78bn (EUR 0.50/share); Q2 FCF -EUR 732m (src 1, 2). Consensus EPS EUR 0.34 (2026) and EUR 0.41 (2027) (src 4, 6). Consensus 2027 already implies ~EUR 3.0bn EBIT, the midpoint of management's 2028 target, so a lot of the AI story is in the numbers. At 23.5x 2027 EPS the stock sits on the 12-peer median forward P/E (23.5x) although more than half its sales are Ericsson-like (16.6x). Valuation: 21x mix-weighted multiple on NTM-at-horizon EPS gives $10.23; the same multiple on the 2028 target midpoint gives $9.29; blended FV $9.90 (about 9% below spot). Base rates (own computation on 308 rolling 12-month windows, 2000-2026, src 20): Nokia's median 12-month price return is -8%, 5th/95th percentiles -56%/+101%, log sd 0.43; the only comparable prior episodes after +80% years were 2007 (next 12m -51% to -64%) and 2013-14 (about -25% to +102%, median ~0). Realized vol is 62% after a 3.6x run from $4.8 to $17.45 and a ~52% fall to $8.37. Event odds: US recession by end-2026 ~8% (oddpool, src 24); FOMC Oct hold 82.5% (src 23). Ladder: lognormal-plus-fat-tail mixture with median ~$10.4 (between FV $9.90 and spot, allowing for estimate-revision momentum from the order book) and log sd 0.46 (between long-run 0.43 and realized 0.62), 20% weight on a 1.6x-wider tail; P(>=spot) = 0.47. Scenario mean ~$10.9. Research limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data estimates/statistics endpoints are paywalled; peer EV/EBITDA is trailing (forward not available at the source); the 2025 20-F was too large to fetch in full; no driver found for today's +6.3% move. Analyst average target $14.97 (src 6) was noted as evidence only and not used in the fair value.
